hook.line: Tomás has the flu, and Doña Gloria wants a full report: what hurts, and where. Spanish says it the *gustar* way.

examples.en: Does your stomach hurt? (to a friend)

examples.es: A don Hernando le duele la rodilla.

rule:
This works like *me gusta*: the body part does the hurting, and the little word in front says whose it is.
*me duele*, *te duele*, *le duele*, *nos duele*, *les duele*
One body part takes *duele*. Two or more take *duelen*: *Me duelen los pies.*
Because *me* already says it's yours, the body part takes *el*, *la*, *los*, *las*, not *mi* or *tu*: *Me duele la cabeza.*
*Un* or *una* means one of several: *Me duele un dedo*, one of my fingers.
smallPrint: Teachers call *doler* a *gustar*-type verb: the body part is the grammatical subject, and the person who feels it is the indirect object.

options: Does your back hurt? (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: A Vale le duelen las piernas.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *duele* or *duelen* and type the whole sentence: *Me ___ los pies.* (My feet hurt.)
yourTurn.why: Two feet, so *duelen*. The verb follows the body part.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *la* or *mi* and type the whole sentence: *Me duele ___ espalda.* (My back hurts.)
yourTurn.why: *Me* already says whose back it is, so just *la*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Does your head hurt?
yourTurn.why: A friend takes *te*, and the head is still *la cabeza*.

yourTurn.answer: A don Hernando le duele la espalda.
accept: A Hernando le duele la espalda.
yourTurn.why: Name him with *a*, keep the *le*, and one back takes *duele*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *Me duele el pie.*
Ask a customer (formal) instead: *¿Te duele algo?*
yourTurn.why: Formal *you* takes *le*, the same word as him or her.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Me* already says whose head it is, so it's *la cabeza*.
Two feet, so *duelen*. The verb follows the body part, not you.
English starts with *my back*. Spanish starts with *me duele* and puts the body part after.

personal: How's your body today? Say one thing that hurts (or *No me duele nada* if you're lucky), then ask a friend about theirs with *¿Te duele…?*
